key_insight: Tabular foundation models are strong on small-to-medium IID benchmarks, but they still lag behind tree-based and deep learning baselines on harder non-IID, large-scale, and high-dimensional tabular problems.
engineering_relevance: For real-world tabular ML systems in science and industry, this paper shows that benchmark choice can strongly change which model appears best, so evaluation must match deployment conditions.
method: Introduced BeyondArena, a unified benchmark covering IID, temporal, and grouped tabular tasks.
Curated 142 datasets across disciplines, feature types, and scale regimes.
Built Data Foundry, a Python framework and metadata schema for standardized dataset curation and benchmarking.
evidence_signal: Across 11 models evaluated on 142 curated datasets, the study finds that performance advantages of tabular foundation models are concentrated on tiny-to-medium IID data, while harder regimes favor traditional methods.
watch_item: Because the benchmark is broad but still curated, results may depend on dataset selection and metadata quality, so adoption will require careful, consistent curation and protocol alignment.
paper_title: Beyond IID: How General Are Tabular Foundation Models, Really?
